newsitem.title: CROATIA: Croatia cenbank buys marks to help kuna liquidity.
newsitem.headline: Croatia cenbank buys marks to help kuna liquidity.

text.p: Croatia's central bank said on Wednesday it bought 65 million German marks at an average of 3.5643 kuna from commercial banks to help their liquidity.
The kuna funds for this purchase will be paid on Friday, ahead of the weekly turnover tax payment by the banks' clients.
The central bank also sold the banking sector four million marks at 3.5652 kuna each, an official told Reuters.

Foreign exchange interventions are more frequent during the summer when the currency inflows from the tourist trade create more demand for kuna, causing its exchange rate to appreciate. -- Kolumbina Bencevic, Zagreb Newsroom, 385-1-4557075
